title: Jtekt India Ltd - 520057 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: JTEKT India FY26 sales grew 11% vs 9% PV market, but full-year EBITDA margin slipped to 7.5% from 7.6% on mix and forex.
summary.overview: FY26 sales grew 11% against passenger vehicle market growth of 9%, helped by GST cuts and new Maruti Suzuki models (e Vitara, Victoris). Second-half EBITDA margin recovered to 8.48% from 7.71%, while H1 margin was 6.3%, leaving the full year at 7.5%. Management attributed the margin drag to product mix (Honda down about 33%, 0.33% impact), a forex accounting effect (0.23%) and US tariffs (0.24%), which it called largely temporary. New capacity (CVJ line 2, MS Gear line 5 and 6, CPS line 3) is still under-utilised, and management expects it to reach full utilisation over 1 to 1.5 years. A Brazil export order from the JTEKT group starts dispatch in May 2026.

segments.name: Customer mix FY26
segments.commentary: Maruti Suzuki rose to 60% of sales from 56%, Toyota fell to 10% from 12%, Honda fell to 5% from 8%, M&M and Tata stayed at 10%, exports rose to 3% from 2%.

segments.name: CVJ (driveline)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about INR 130 crore per management; line 2 (from Nov 2025, capacity about 370,000 units) is 27% utilised, line 1 about 83%. Full two-line volume targeted at about INR 250 crore with the Maruti EV MPV from October 2026.

segments.name: Manual gear (MS Gear)
segments.commentary: Line 5 at Dharuhera is at 106% utilisation; line 6 is at 21%, expected to reach 60% then 80-90%. Company holds 40-45% share of manual gear business.

segments.name: CPS
segments.commentary: Line 3 at Bawal is about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.

guidance_outlook: Management expects new capacity to be fully utilised within 1 to 1.5 years, depending on market conditions.

Illustrative FY27 incremental revenue: about INR 400 crore from 10% market growth plus INR 75-100 crore exports, so about INR 500 crore; management referred to INR 800 crore total extra business across FY26 and FY27 (INR 300 crore achieved in FY26). Management declined to give formal FY27 guidance.
Brazil (Stellantis) order to start dispatch in May 2026, about 70,000 units in FY27 (management cited 70,000 this year and 100,000-150,000 next year), with potential to reach 5 lakh units per year.
Honda's EV SUV from Tapukara expected around December 2026, optimistically about 40,000 units and about INR 100 crore business for JTEKT.

Management expects the margin pressures from product mix and forex accounting to be temporary; US tariff reduced from 50% to 10% after the Supreme Court ruling, which management expects to lift US exports.
Capex for FY27 expected to be lower than the last two years; about INR 100 crore more for the Gujarat plant (total committed about INR 250 crore, INR 130 crore spent), plus normal capex.
capex_capacity: CVJ line 2 commissioned November 2025; capacity about 7.54 lakh units per annum (about 3.8 lakh vehicle sets); line 2 utilisation 27%, line 1 about 83%; work started on a third CVJ line.
MS Gear line 5 at Dharuhera 106% utilised; MS Gear line 6 at 21%; MS Gear line 4 at Chennai for export not yet started (SOP pending); capacity about 3.5-4 lakh per MS Gear line.
CPS line 3 at Bawal about 50% utilised; capacity about 5 lakh units per line.
Chennai rack and pinion line for Brazil export with installed capacity about 4 lakh units.
Gujarat plant committed at about INR 250 crore; about INR 130 crore spent so far, and about INR 100 crore further spend expected over 1-2 years.
CWIP of about INR 411 crore; management asked analysts to track CWIP as it will weigh on ratios for 1-2 years.
demand_pricing: PV market grew 9% in FY26, with 16.7% growth in H2 after GST cut (28% to 18% for small cars; 50% to 40% for larger ones); H1 growth was only 1.6%.
Honda's passenger vehicle business fell about 30%, reducing JTEKT's sales (almost 100% supplier to Honda); Renault-Nissan export models fell about 16%, Toyota about 4%.
Raw material cost pass-through to customers is back-to-back with a time lag, per management.
Competition in CVJ from GKN-linked and other suppliers, which hold over 60% of Maruti's business; management targets at least 15% CVJ share.
Management said it is not supplying Renault's Duster.

qa_highlights.question: Why have gross margins declined from 29% to 27% over two years, and how should they trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margin was 6.3% and H2 8.48%; net variable cost drag of 0.18% came from a 0.33% mix effect (Honda, Renault-Nissan, Toyota down; Maruti GST-driven models higher), 0.23% forex accounting effect and 0.24% US tariffs, offset by export gains and lower warranty. Management called these temporary.

qa_highlights.question: Has Toyota's Bidadi third line commenced, and what is Toyota's revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bidadi line had not commenced per its understanding; a new Maharashtra facility is expected in H1 FY29, lifting Toyota capacity to about 1 lakh vehicles. JTEKT is the only steering supplier to Toyota.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for other driveline products beyond CVJ and hub bearings for JTEKT's group?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete plan is finalised; management said it needs 1-1.5 years to stabilise CVJ first. It noted export opportunities for CVJ parts to group entities.

qa_highlights.question: Update on the INR 1,000 crore top-line addition by FY27 and whether revenue can double in 3-4 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 300 crore was added in FY26; with 10% market growth and INR 75-100 crore exports, about INR 500 crore more is possible in FY27 (about INR 800 crore total). It declined to share a formal business plan and said growth depends on the market.

qa_highlights.question: Expected FY27 capex and ROCE trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex will be lower than the last two years, with about INR 100 crore for Gujarat plus normal capex. ROCE excluding CWIP is above 11%, and full utilisation should push it back toward earlier levels (about 16-17%).

qa_highlights.question: Driveline pipeline, CVJ margins and fixed asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: CVJ margins are better than most MS Gear products and it is 100% localised. Target fixed asset turnover is about 3x overall; CVJ is lower (about 1.5x), CPS 2.5-3x, manual gear 2-2.5x.

qa_highlights.question: Potential for exports to US and Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Brazil is the first step, with a Stellantis order, and that a further order could follow once quality and cost are established. No firm US or Europe plan was given.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the H2 run-rate (8.48%) holding and on the forex and mix effects not recurring.
Ramp-up of new capacity: CVJ line 2 at 27% and CPS line 3 at 50% utilisation; delays in the Maruti EV MPV launch (October 2026) and Honda's EV SUV (December 2026) would push out volume.
ROCE at about 10% with CWIP of INR 411 crore; fixed asset turnover has fallen from above 4x to about 2.2x per analyst.
Honda and Renault-Nissan export volume declines; mix shift toward lower-margin Maruti models.
Brazil ramp (70,000 units this year, up to 5 lakh units) and US tariff relief, which were not yet quantified in guidance.
Rising state power tariffs and reciprocal tariffs on US exports.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid and detailed on margin pressure and calls the drag temporary, but it was evasive on forward numbers, declining to share FY27 business plan or formal guidance. Confidence is high on the Brazil order and the ramp-up of the Maruti EV programmes, and it deferred on Toyota Bidadi and new product plans.

We expect that whatever capacities we have set up will be 100% utilized over the next 1 year or maybe 1.5 years.
CWIP is a major thing which you must keep in mind.
We are currently supplying to 100% of Maruti EV business at this point of time.
